mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, which produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below its 5-year median (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate exceeding 2.0% signals aggressive monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate weakening consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime, a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals labor market deterioration, reducing corporate hiring and profit growth, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE < 4.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) indicate robust consumer demand for housing, boosting construction sector activity and corporate earnings, which produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 5-year median (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 indicates manufacturing contraction, signaling economic slowdown and reduced corporate profitability, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100 (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decreases in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicate an overheating economy with tightening monetary policy, which triggers equity sell-offs and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises and UNRATE falls (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime, a decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) signals potential monetary policy easing, which reduces discount rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive when CPIAUCSL declines and CPIAUCSL > 2.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.
